1  MFA No. 1308 of 2018 NO.45/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, &
ADDITIONAL MACT, KARKALA, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION ETC.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.45/2017 dated 11.10.2017, seeking enhancement of the compensation, on the file of the Senior Civil Judge &
AMACT, Karkala.
2. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.12,55,333/-, whereby the Tribunal had awarded an amount of Rs.4,68,980/-.

This is the case of the claimant that on 18.02.2016 at about 12.30 noon when the claimant was riding his motor cycle, one maruthi omni car came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, he had sustained injuries.

As per the Ex.P-7 wound certificate, the claimant NC: 2023:KHC:41462 had sustained abrasions over dorsum of right foot, dorsum of left foot which are simple in nature, scrapped lacerated wounds over outer aspect of left ankle with tissue loss,
tenderness over low back with underlying burst compression fracture of 3rd lumbar vertebral body with retropulsion, fracture of transverse process of 1st and 2nd lumbar vertebra on left side, fracture of transverse process of 3rd lumbar vertebra bilaterally, fracture of lamina of 3rd lumbar vertebra on right side, fracture of spinous process of 4th lumbar vertebra and left psoas haematoma giving rise to paraplegia i.e., paralysis of both the lower limbs which are grievous in nature.

Considering the injuries sustained by the claimant, the doctor has given the certificate that he had sustained 20%
disability to the spine part of the body.

The Tribunal considering the disability, taking 1/3rd of it,
had considered 7% disability.
When it comes to the income, it is case of the claimant that he is earning an amount of Rs.30,000/- per month and the court below had taken an amount of Rs.12,000/-.
Considering the disability at 7% had granted an amount of NC: 2023:KHC:41462 Rs.1,51,200/- under the head of loss of loss of future income.
Towards pain and agony an amount of Rs.60,000/- was granted.

Towards loss of amenities an amount of Rs.30,000/-, towards Attendant,
Nourishment, Food and Conveyance an amount of Rs.8,000/- and Rs.5,000/- respectively.
Towards medical expenses an amount of Rs.1,73,580/- was granted.
Towards loss of income during the laid up period, an amount of Rs.41,200/- was granted.
Altogether a compensation of an amount of Rs.4,68,980/- was granted by the Tribunal.
3. Learned counsel for the claimant submits that when there is injury to the spinal cord which is a major part of the body, the court ought not to have taken 1/3rd of it.

It is submitted that when the matter came up before this court, as per the orders passed by this court, examined by the Medical Board, Udupi and it has Certified that the disability is at 20% and disability is not likely to improve.

2
It is submitted that as it is going to have an impact on his future prospects, the court below ought to NC: 2023:KHC:41462 have considered the future prospects.
He submits that instead of taking an amount of Rs.30,000/-, the court below had taken only an amount of Rs.12,000/- as income.
Even under the other heads also the compensation that was granted by the Tribunal was not reasonable.

4. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that they have satisfied with the award, but however it is submitted that when there was no proper evidence with regard to the income, the court below ought not to have taken an amount of Rs.12,000/-.
Further it is submitted that they are not entitled for future prospects as there was no evidence on record to show it and further no grounds are made out for enhancement of the compensation.
5. Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.

First coming NC: 2023:KHC:41462 to the income of the claimant, it is the case of the Insurance Company though they have not preferred the appeal, this court has to look at award while enhancing the compensation.
The income that was taken in this case is excessive and without any evidence, the court can as well correct the same.
In this case, the insurance company has already satisfied the award.
In that case, when they are not aggrieved by the award passed by the Tribunal this court is not inclined to go into the said aspect and further consider an amount of Rs.12,000/-.
In every case of disability considering the future prospects will not arise, unless and until the percentage of the disability is more.

Hence in this case, this court is not inclined to consider future prospects, hence considering the income at an amount of Rs.12,000/- x 12 x Multiplier 15 x 20/100 an amount of Rs.4,32,000/- is granted towards of loss of income due to disability.
Towards pain and agony, the court below had rightly granted an amount of Rs.60,000/- and this court do not find any reasons to enhance the same.
Under the head of loss of amenities in NC: 2023:KHC:41462 life, the court below had granted an amount of Rs.30,000/-.
Considering the spinal cord injury, this court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Towards Attendant, Nourishment and Transport, this court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.20,000/-.

Then coming to the loss of income during the laid up period, the court below had granted an amount of Rs.41,200/- and toward medical expenses the court below had granted an amount of Rs.1,73,580/-, under these heads, this court do not find any reasons to interfere.

6. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V. MEKALA -vs- M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER 1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.
